# Certora 8.19.2: second migration batch

32 additional configurations select 8.19.2, bringing the repository to **40 of 41**. This covers all Delay, Safe and Governor configurations, and four additional Roles configurations. The original CI matrix remains 34 configurations: **33 use 8.19.2 and one remains on 7.31.0**. All seven manual configurations now use 8.19.2.

## Evidence

The candidate jobs are complete, uncached cloud proofs. Every candidate result node is verified, including sanity and the existing existential witnesses. Archived sources match [`b86c679`](https://github.com/term-finance/zodiac-modifier-roles-v1/tree/b86c67923e6437ebc05df34d79c0c812ffc9eb82/packages/evm/certora). The [machine-readable record](8.19.2-second-batch.json) retains compiler/backend versions, source and archive hashes, coverage counts, diagnostics, and all 41 CLI selections.

The 24 CI baselines other than Governor voting come from the passing [7.31.0 main run](https://github.com/term-finance/zodiac-modifier-roles-v1/actions/runs/37650684284) at `b78b57e`. Governor voting and the 7 migrated manual configurations have fresh uncached 7.31.0 baselines from merged main at `ffb8558`. Every baseline input is compared against its candidate archive. The newer [main run](https://github.com/term-finance/zodiac-modifier-roles-v1/actions/runs/38446218321) also passed all 34 jobs before this branch.

**Governor end-to-end is a completed 8.x improvement over an incomplete 7.x proof.** Its 7.x functional witness and 22 leaves verify, but the non-vacuity sanity check times out. The 8.x candidate verifies all 24 leaves, including that sanity check and the new assertion companion. The existing 3,600-second solver timeout, model, compiled scene, reported calls, resolved targets and havoc scopes are unchanged. The 7.x timeout is explicitly retained in the record; it is not counted as a passing baseline or omitted from coverage.

All **2,866 baseline rule/method/sanity groups** remain, with 3,051 groups on 8.x. Verified leaves increase from **1,658 to 1,841**. No original reported call is removed and no call-resolution warning is added. Two additional reported calls appear in the new assertion subrules of the Safe fallback-handler witnesses; they retain the existing explicit dispatcher and `ASSERT_FALSE` default.

The CVL edits add 74 `assert true` companions before existing `satisfy` statements. These preserve pessimistic checks and sanity alongside existential witnesses, as described in [Certora's satisfy documentation](https://docs.certora.com/en/latest/docs/cvl/statements.html#satisfy-statements). Parametric rules produce 179 additional assertion groups; some rules already had such a group. Six additional groups are constructor sanity checks. Existing assertions, witness predicates, assumptions, filters, summaries, compiler settings, scene links, recursion limits and loop bounds stay intact. No Solidity, harness, dependency, configuration or CI matrix is changed.

## Scope of the claims

These are compatibility proofs of the existing conditional models. Their assumptions remain visible in the pinned specifications:

- **Delay:** owner/module authority, queue provenance, pause behavior, signed settings and the existing composed Safe paths. The existing signature stubs, authorized-caller relations, scene links, guards, bounded queue/hash behavior and dispatch defaults remain.
- **Safe 1.3.0 and 1.4.1:** entry paths, self-calls, handler behavior, configuration guards, module behavior and signed settings. Existing signature summaries, configured guard/module/owner premises, external-call abstractions and recursion/loop bounds remain. Signed witnesses do not independently prove signature validation.
- **Roles:** configuration integrity, guard sufficiency, role-configuration sufficiency and whether the configured veto call lands on Delay. Guard installation, target/owner relations, role configuration, caller membership and bounded calldata assumptions are unchanged. The role-configuration suite retains its witnesses for limits of role configuration without the guard, including multisend behavior.
- **Governor:** proposal threshold, settings, vote accounting, tally stability, veto behavior and the composed TERM-holder proposal/vote/execute witness. The linked TERM scene, historical-vote/signature summaries, external-call abstractions, optimistic hashing and loop bounds remain. These runs do not establish the correctness of every summarized external dependency.

The inventory accounts for 41 specs in 41 contexts and issues **zero semantic dependency-closure certificates**. Deployment bindings, abstraction refinement, specification adequacy and mutation coverage remain separate obligations. No negative-control proof is claimed in this batch.

## Diagnostics

The record distinguishes inherited diagnostics, diagnostics outside the exercised methods, and analysis whose optimization was already disabled. No analysis flag or scope filter was changed to silence a diagnostic.

- The six manual Safe/Delay comparisons retain the same `execTransaction` call-graph failure on **both uncached versions**, including signed paths. Their reported calls and full result coverage are preserved. Certora [falls back to another call-graph analysis](https://github.com/Certora/CertoraProver/blob/8.19.2/src/main/kotlin/analysis/icfg/CallGraphBuilder.kt#L4485-L4538). Other Safe contexts report it only for unexercised `execTransaction`; that exclusion is checked against the actual method instances, specs and reported calls.
- Safe `getStorageAt` storage-analysis/splitting diagnostics concern an unexercised method. Governor scenes also retain an internal-function detection diagnostic in TERM's unexercised `send`. No method or contract was removed from the compiled scene.
- Governor voting's five active voting methods report the same storage-analysis/splitting failures in its **fresh 7.31.0 baseline and 8.19.2 candidate**. Both complete successfully with identical compiled methods and reported calls. The spec uses Solidity getters and contains no CVL storage hooks. Governor settings already disables storage splitting on both versions and also has no storage hooks. The [storage-analysis implementation retains a failure only for later consumers](https://github.com/Certora/CertoraProver/blob/8.19.2/src/main/kotlin/analysis/storage/StorageAnalysis.kt#L4195-L4203), and [storage-splitting failures can affect runtime](https://github.com/Certora/CertoraProver/blob/8.19.2/src/main/kotlin/analysis/split/StorageSplitter.kt#L71-L90). These are recorded limitations, not clean analysis logs.
- Call-trace argument-display errors remain in some suites. The old cached Governor settings and veto baselines have verified sanity results whose trace generation failed; the 8.19.2 candidates have no report-node errors. Thousands of older display-annotation warnings are absent on 8.x. These reporting improvements do not discharge semantic-closure obligations.
- `Roles-setTxNonceRoleConfigSufficient` logs one background-task shutdown timeout **after** reporting all 15 proof rules verified, 16/16 processed rules and zero pending tasks. All 41 result leaves, including sanity, are verified and their outputs are archived. The pinned [background-coroutine implementation](https://github.com/Certora/CertoraProver/blob/8.19.2/lib/GeneralUtils/src/main/kotlin/parallel/coroutines/BackgroundCoroutineScope.kt#L157-L192) emits this message while waiting for background jobs after the main block finishes. This is recorded separately from solver timeouts; the result reports zero proof timeouts and errors.

## Remaining on 7.31.0

| Configuration | Why it is held back |
| --- | --- |
| `Roles-setTxNonceGuardAndRoleConfig.conf` | Reported library-call inventory differs; the 8.x model appears to omit selector bytes that native EVM execution preserves. Investigate Permissions.keyForFunctions before promotion. |

The isolated attempts and their snapshot states are recorded in the JSON. A green candidate does not by itself establish model compatibility. Their experimental CVL changes are not adopted. New, unvalidated configuration names also continue to default to 7.31.0.

The held-back Roles suite has two disappearing `AUTO havoc` library-call warnings; a fresh uncached 7.31.0 rerun confirms the original warnings. The 8.x witness instead inlines `Permissions.keyForFunctions`. With target `0x2546` and selector `0x46ba2307`, its reported return and pre-solver expression omit the selector contribution. Native EVM execution of the unchanged `Permissions.sol`, compiled with Solidity 0.8.6, optimizer runs 1 and Berlin, returns `0x254646ba23070000000000000000` as expected. A separate complete cloud experiment changes only `-enableMemorySplit false`: every result is verified, but the pre-solver expression still omits the selector. That configuration change is therefore not adopted. This warrants further investigation of translation, analysis and scene configuration; it is not evidence that a prover patch is necessarily required. No replacement summary or narrowed assumption is introduced to obtain a pass.

## Local checks

`python3 packages/evm/certora/toolchain_test.py` passes all four routing/runner tests. All migrated configurations compile locally with 8.19.2 and their original Solidity versions, including mixed 0.7.6/0.8.6/0.8.20 scenes. The cloud checks use the entire configuration with basic sanity and no rule/method selection overrides.
